title: Kanchenjunga at breakfast
standfirst: A border culture unlike anywhere else in India, with the third-highest mountain in the world above it.

blocks.heading: The mountain hides by noon
paras: Kanchenjunga is clear at dawn and gone by late morning for most of the year.
Every house we use is chosen for its aspect, and the mornings are held for the mountain rather than for driving.

blocks.heading: North Sikkim, with time
blocks.caption: Permits and long drives; worth it with the days to spare.
paras: The north is the most remarkable part of the state and the hardest to reach, with permits and long mountain roads.
We only suggest it when there are days to spare, and we arrange the permits well ahead.

blocks.heading: Monasteries and weaving
blocks.caption: A culture that sits between Tibet, Nepal and Bengal.
paras: The monasteries here are working rather than visited, and the weaving traditions are still domestic.
Visits are arranged rather than turned up to, which is the difference between watching and being shown.

blocks.heading: Questions members ask
blocks.intro: The ones that come up nearly every time.

a: March to May for rhododendron; October and November for the clearest mountain views.
Fly to Bagdogra and drive up, or take the helicopter when weather allows. The drive is four to five hours.
For the north and for several border areas, yes. They take time and we handle them in advance.

blocks.heading: We are ready when you are
paras: Every itinerary starts with a conversation about what you actually want from the days, and works backwards to houses, guides and timing from there.
